at kaste op.explanation: "At kaste op" means "to throw up". It is made of kaste (to throw) and op (up): Han kastede op (He threw up).

sentence.da: Han er syg og vil **kaste op**.
sentence.en: He is sick and wants to throw up.

at kende.explanation: "At kende" means "to know (a person or place)", or to be familiar with something: Jeg kender Anna (I know Anna). To know a fact, use at vide (to know), as in Jeg ved, at hun bor her (I know that she lives here).

forms.en: I have known (a person or place)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **kende** dine venner bedre.
sentence.en: I would like to know your friends better.

at kigge.explanation: "At kigge" means "to look": Kig her! (Look here!). It is often followed by på (at): Jeg kigger på billedet (I am looking at the picture). In a store, you may hear Jeg kigger bare (I'm just looking).

sentence.da: Jeg vil bare **kigge** på tøjet i butikken.
sentence.en: I just want to look at the clothes in the store.

at klemme.explanation: "At klemme" means "to squeeze" or "to pinch", for example a lemon or your finger in a door: Jeg klemte fingeren i døren (I pinched my finger in the door).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **klemme** en citron over fisken.
sentence.en: I want to squeeze a lemon over the fish.

at klæde sig på.explanation: "At klæde sig på" means "to get dressed". The small word sig (oneself) changes with the person: du klæder dig på (you get dressed), han klæder sig på (he gets dressed). To put on one item, say at tage en jakke på (to put on a jacket).

sentence.en: The children have to get dressed now.

at koge.explanation: "At koge" means "to boil", or to cook in boiling water, for example eggs, pasta and potatoes: Vandet koger (The water is boiling). For cooking food in general, use at lave mad (to cook): Jeg laver mad (I am cooking).

sentence.en: I am going to boil potatoes in water.

at komme.explanation: "At komme" means "to come", for arriving and for being on the way: Jeg kommer nu (I am coming now). Hvor kommer du fra? means "Where are you from?". It is also used for what will happen next: Det kommer til at regne (It is going to rain).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme** til din fest i morgen.
sentence.en: I will come to your party tomorrow.

at komme hjem.explanation: "At komme hjem" means "to come home", to arrive at home: Hvornår kommer du hjem? (When will you get home?). To say you are leaving for home, use at tage hjem (to go home): Jeg tager hjem nu (I am going home now).

sentence.en: I want to come home tonight.

at komme ind.explanation: "At komme ind" means "to come in" or "to get in": Kom ind! (Come in!). Vi kom ikke ind i klubben means "We could not get into the club".

sentence.en: You can come in now.

at komme ned.explanation: "At komme ned" means "to come down", for example down the stairs or from a higher floor: Kom ned og spis! (Come down and eat!).

sentence.en: Can you come down the stairs?

at komme op.explanation: "At komme op" means "to come up", and also "to get up", for example from a chair: Han kom op af stolen (He got up from the chair). Kom op! can also mean "Come on!". To get out of bed, Danes usually say at stå op (to get up).

forms.en: I have come up / gotten up

sentence.da: Jeg skal **komme op** af sengen nu.
sentence.en: I have to get out of bed now.

at komme tilbage.explanation: "At komme tilbage" means "to come back" or "to return". Jeg kommer snart tilbage means "I will be back soon". Hvornår kommer du tilbage? means "When are you coming back?".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme tilbage** til Danmark næste år.
sentence.en: I want to come back to Denmark next year.

at komme ud.explanation: "At komme ud" means "to come out" or "to get out", of a room, house or building: Kom ud! means "Come out!" and Han kommer ud af skolen means "He comes out of the school".

forms.en: I have come out / gotten out

sentence.en: I want to get out of the house.

at koste.explanation: "At koste" means "to cost". It is mostly used with det (it) or de (they): Hvad koster det? (How much does it cost?). Because a thing does the costing, the forms above start with det (it) instead of jeg (I).

sentence.da: Den nye bluse vil **koste** hundrede kroner.
sentence.en: The new blouse will cost a hundred kroner.

at kunne.explanation: "At kunne" means "can / to be able to". Another action word follows straight after it, with no at in between: Jeg kan svømme (I can swim), Kan du hjælpe mig? (Can you help me?).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **kunne** svømme som en fisk.
sentence.en: I would like to be able to swim like a fish.

at kunne lide.explanation: "At kunne lide" means "to like": Jeg kan lide kaffe (I like coffee). With a person, you usually add godt (well): Jeg kan godt lide dig (I like you). To say you do not like something, add ikke (not): Jeg kan ikke lide det (I don't like it).

sentence.en: You will like the food here.

at købe.explanation: "At købe" means "to buy": Jeg køber brød (I am buying bread). Add for and the price to say what you paid: Jeg købte den for hundrede kroner (I bought it for a hundred kroner).

sentence.en: I would like to buy a ticket.

at købe ind.explanation: "At købe ind" means "to buy groceries", or to do your shopping, mostly for food and things for the home. At købe (to buy) is more general. You often hear Jeg skal ud og købe ind (I am going out to shop).

sentence.en: I need to buy groceries for dinner.

at køre.explanation: "At køre" means "to drive", or to ride in a vehicle: Jeg kører i bil (I go by car). It is also used for a bus or train that runs: Bussen kører hver time (The bus runs every hour). For a bike, you usually say at cykle (to cycle).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **køre** bilen til arbejde i morgen.
sentence.en: I want to drive the car to work tomorrow.

at køre hjem.explanation: "At køre hjem" means "to drive home", and works for any vehicle that takes you there, such as a car or a bus. For going on foot, use at gå hjem (to walk home).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **køre hjem**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to drive home.

en kage.explanation: "En kage" means "a cake", but Danes also use kage for pastries and other sweet baked treats. At bage en kage means "to bake a cake".

sentence.en: We eat cake for my birthday.

en kalender.explanation: "En kalender" means "a calendar". Jeg tjekker min kalender means "I check my calendar".

sentence.en: I write the meeting in my calendar.

en kanin.explanation: "En kanin" means "a rabbit". Do not mix it up with en hare (a hare). Kaninen spiser en gulerod means "The rabbit eats a carrot".

sentence.da: En **kanin** har lange ører og hopper rundt.
sentence.en: A rabbit has long ears and hops around.

en kartoffel.explanation: "En kartoffel" means "a potato". You can say kogte kartofler (boiled potatoes) or stegte kartofler (fried potatoes).

sentence.da: Jeg skræller en **kartoffel** og koger den.
sentence.en: I peel a potato and boil it.

en kasket.explanation: "En kasket" means "a cap", the kind with a peak at the front, like a baseball cap. It is not en hue (a knit wool hat) or en hat (a hat with a brim).

sentence.da: Han har en **kasket** på i solen.
sentence.en: He has a cap on in the sun.

en kat.explanation: "En kat" means "a cat". Katten sover means "The cat is sleeping", and Jeg har to katte means "I have two cats".

sentence.da: Min **kat** siger mjav og drikker mælk.
sentence.en: My cat says meow and drinks milk.

en kiks.explanation: "En kiks" means "a biscuit" or "a cracker". En småkage (a small sweet cookie) is a different thing.

sentence.en: I eat a cracker with cheese.

en kilometer.explanation: "En kilometer" means "a kilometer", which is 1,000 meters. Fem kilometer means "five kilometers". Speed is measured in kilometer i timen (kilometers per hour).

sentence.en: It is three kilometers to the station.

en kind.explanation: "En kind" means "a cheek". Røde kinder means "red cheeks", and et kys på kinden means "a kiss on the cheek".

sentence.da: Hun giver mig et kys på min **kind**.
sentence.en: She gives me a kiss on my cheek.

en kiosk.explanation: "En kiosk" means "a kiosk", a small shop that sells drinks, sweets, newspapers and snacks. It is smaller than et supermarked (a supermarket).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en avis i en **kiosk**.
sentence.en: I buy a newspaper at a kiosk.

en kirke.explanation: "En kirke" means "a church", and i kirken means "in the church". Do not confuse it with en kirkegård (a cemetery), which contains the word kirke but is a place with graves.

sentence.da: Der er en stor **kirke** i byen.
sentence.en: There is a big church in the town.

en kjole.explanation: "En kjole" means "a dress". You can build words from it, such as en festkjole (a party dress) and en sommerkjole (a summer dress).

sentence.da: Hun har en lang **kjole** på til festen.
sentence.en: She is wearing a long dress to the party.

en klasse.explanation: "En klasse" means "a class", both the group of pupils and the classroom. Danish schools count the school years as classes: 2. klasse means "second grade".

sentence.da: Der er tyve børn i min **klasse**.
sentence.en: There are twenty children in my class.

en klinik.explanation: "En klinik" means "a clinic", a place where you see a doctor or dentist without staying overnight. A hospital, where people can stay overnight, is et sygehus or "et hospital".

sentence.da: Jeg ser en læge på en **klinik**.
sentence.en: I see a doctor at a clinic.

en kniv.explanation: "En kniv" means "a knife". Kniven er skarp means "The knife is sharp", and en kniv og en gaffel means "a knife and a fork".

sentence.en: I cut bread with a knife.

en ko.explanation: "En ko" means "a cow". Køerne spiser græs means "The cows eat grass".

sentence.en: I see a cow in the field.

en kok.explanation: "En kok" means "a chef" or "a cook". Do not mix it up with at koge (to boil). Kokken laver maden means "The chef makes the food".

sentence.da: Min bror er **kok** på en restaurant.
sentence.en: My brother is a chef at a restaurant.

en kollega.explanation: "En kollega" means "a colleague". Mine kolleger means "my colleagues".

sentence.da: Min **kollega** og jeg arbejder sammen på kontoret.
sentence.en: My colleague and I work together in the office.

en koncert.explanation: "En koncert" means "a concert". At gå til koncert means "to go to a concert", and Danish leaves out the word for "a" there.

sentence.en: We listen to music at a concert.

en kone.explanation: "En kone" means "a wife". For a woman in general, use en kvinde (a woman), not kone, which only means a married partner.

sentence.en: My wife is at home today.

en kop.explanation: "En kop" means "a cup", mostly for hot drinks: en kop kaffe (a cup of coffee) or en kop te (a cup of tea). Cold drinks go in et glas (a glass).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **kop** kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like a cup of coffee.

en krokodille.explanation: "En krokodille" means "a crocodile". Krokodillen åbner munden means "The crocodile opens its mouth".

sentence.en: A crocodile lives in the river.

en krone.explanation: "En krone" means "a crown", the money used in Denmark. After a number, you say kroner: tyve kroner means "twenty crowns". The short written form is kr.

sentence.en: I only have one krone.

en krop.explanation: "En krop" means "a body". Jeg har ondt i kroppen means "My whole body aches". When one body part hurts, Danish says "the" where English says "my": Jeg har ondt i hovedet means "My head hurts".

sentence.da: Min **krop** er meget træt i dag.
sentence.en: My body is very tired today.

en kuffert.explanation: "En kuffert" means "a suitcase". At pakke en kuffert means "to pack a suitcase", and "at pakke ud" means "to unpack".

sentence.en: I have clothes in my suitcase.

en kuglepen.explanation: "En kuglepen" means "a ballpoint pen". It is built from kugle (ball) and pen (pen), because of the tiny ball at the tip.

sentence.da: Jeg skriver et brev med en blå **kuglepen**.
sentence.en: I write a letter with a blue ballpoint pen.

en kusine.explanation: "En kusine" means "a female cousin". Danish has two words where English has one: en fætter means "a male cousin".

sentence.da: Min **kusine** er datter af min tante.
sentence.en: My cousin is my aunt's daughter.

en kvinde.explanation: "En kvinde" means "a woman". Use en pige (a girl) for a girl or a young woman.

sentence.en: That woman is my mother.

en kvittering.explanation: "En kvittering" means "a receipt". Skal du have kvitteringen? means "Do you want the receipt?". En bon is a shorter everyday word for it.

sentence.da: Jeg betalte i butikken og fik en **kvittering**.
sentence.en: I paid in the shop and got a receipt.

en kæreste.explanation: "En kæreste" means "a partner" in the romantic sense: a boyfriend or girlfriend you are not necessarily married to. It comes from kær (dear).

sentence.en: I live together with my partner.

et kilo.explanation: "Et kilo" means "a kilo", short for et kilogram (a kilogram). After a number it stays kilo: to kilo (two kilos).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have et **kilo** æbler.
sentence.en: I would like a kilo of apples.

et klaver.explanation: "Et klaver" means "a piano". Danish leaves out the word the when you play it: at spille klaver (to play the piano). Klaver is the normal word, though et piano (a piano) is also understood.

sentence.en: She plays the piano at home.

et knæ.explanation: "Et knæ" means "a knee". The k is pronounced, so say k-næ. For example, Jeg har ondt i knæet (My knee hurts).

sentence.en: She fell and hurt her knee.

et kodeord.explanation: "Et kodeord" means "a password". It is literally a code word, from en kode (a code) and et ord (a word).

sentence.en: I forgot my password.

et kontor.explanation: "Et kontor" means "an office". For example, Hun er på kontoret (She is at the office). Et postkontor (a post office) is built on the same word.

sentence.da: Hun arbejder ved en computer på et **kontor**.
sentence.en: She works at a computer in an office.

et kort.explanation: "Et kort" means both a map and "a card", so the context tells you which. Et kort over Danmark is a map of Denmark, and "et kreditkort" is a credit card. Without et, kort can also mean "short".

sentence.da: Jeg kigger på et **kort** over byen.
sentence.en: I look at a map of the town.

et kæledyr.explanation: "Et kæledyr" means "a pet", an animal you keep at home for company, such as a dog or cat. It is made of at kæle (to cuddle) and et dyr (an animal).

sentence.en: We have a dog as a pet.

et køkken.explanation: "Et køkken" means "a kitchen", the room where you cook food. It can also mean a style of cooking: det danske køkken means "Danish cuisine".

sentence.da: Jeg laver aftensmad i et lille **køkken**.
sentence.en: I make dinner in a small kitchen.

et køleskab.explanation: "Et køleskab" means "a fridge". It is made of køle (cool) and et skab (a cupboard), so it is literally a cooling cupboard.

sentence.en: The milk is in the fridge.

kaffe.explanation: "Kaffe" means "coffee". To order it, you can say en kaffe, tak (a coffee, please) or just kaffe, tak. To invite someone, say Skal vi have en kop kaffe? (Shall we have a cup of coffee?).

sentence.en: Do you want a cup of coffee?

kakao.explanation: "Kakao" means "cocoa" or "hot chocolate", the drink as well as the powder. You can ask for en varm kakao (a hot cocoa).

sentence.en: The children drink hot cocoa.

kan du gentage det?.explanation: "Kan du gentage det?" means "Can you repeat that?" and is a polite way to ask when you did not catch what someone said. Add tak (please) to be extra polite: Kan du gentage det, tak?

sentence.en: Sorry, can you repeat that?

kan jeg betale med kort?.explanation: "Kan jeg betale med kort?" means "can I pay by card?". Med means "with" and kort means "card". For cash, swap med kort for kontant (in cash): Kan jeg betale kontant? (Can I pay in cash?).

sentence.en: Hi, can I pay by card?

kan jeg købe ...?.explanation: "Kan jeg købe ...?" means "can I buy ...?". Kan jeg means "can I", and you put what you want in place of the dots. Danes also often say jeg vil gerne have... (I would like...).

sentence.da: Undskyld, **kan jeg købe** en kop kaffe?
sentence.en: Excuse me, can I buy a cup of coffee?

kartofler.explanation: "Kartofler" means "potatoes". Say how they are cooked by putting a word in front, as in kogte kartofler (boiled potatoes) or stegte kartofler (fried potatoes).

sentence.en: French fries are made of potatoes.

ked af.explanation: "Ked af" means "sorry" or "sad". Jeg er ked af det can mean either "I am sorry" or "I am sad", and the situation tells you which. Undskyld (sorry, excuse me) is the quick word for small things, such as bumping into someone.

forms.en: I am sorry about it / I am sad about it.

forms.da: Jeg er ked af, at jeg kom for sent.
forms.en: I am sorry that I came too late.

sentence.da: Hun græder og er **ked af** det.
sentence.en: She is crying and she is sad.

ked af det.explanation: "Ked af det" means "sad" or "upset". It is used after er (am, is, are). Jeg er ked af det can also mean "I am sorry", so the situation tells you which.

sentence.da: Barnet græder og er **ked af det**.
sentence.en: The child is crying and is sad.

kedelig.explanation: "Kedelig" means "boring", for things and for people. It can also mean "unfortunate": Det er kedeligt often means "That is too bad". If you are bored yourself, say Jeg keder mig (I am bored).

sentence.en: That film is very boring.

ketchup.explanation: "Ketchup" means "ketchup". You do not count it, so you say noget ketchup (some ketchup).

sentence.da: Vil du have **ketchup** til pommes frites?
sentence.en: Do you want ketchup with the fries?

kina.explanation: "Kina" means "China". Compare Jeg bor i Kina (I live in China) with Jeg rejser til Kina (I am traveling to China).

sentence.da: **Kina** er et stort land i Asien.
sentence.en: China is a big country in Asia.

kinesisk.explanation: "Kinesisk" means "Chinese", for the language and for things from China, and it is written with a small letter. Kinesisk mad means "Chinese food", and "Jeg taler kinesisk" means "I speak Chinese".

sentence.en: In China, people speak Chinese.

klar.explanation: "Klar" means "ready" or "clear". Er du klar? means "Are you ready?" and "Det er klart" means "Of course" or "That is clear". Do not mix it up with færdig (finished), which says something is done, not that you are ready.

sentence.en: Are you ready to go?

klokken.explanation: "Klokken" means "o'clock" and literally "the clock". Klokken er tre means "It is three o'clock", and you also use it for when something happens: Vi mødes klokken otte (We meet at eight o'clock). In writing, it is shortened to kl.

sentence.en: It is eight o'clock in the morning.

klokken er fem.explanation: "Klokken er fem" means "it is five o'clock". To give the time on the hour, say klokken er and the number. When you answer Hvad er klokken? (What time is it?) briefly, Danes often leave out klokken er and just say fem.

sentence.en: It's five o'clock now.

kogt.explanation: "Kogt" means "boiled". Compare stegt (fried): en kogt kartoffel (a boiled potato) is cooked in water, but en stegt kartoffel (a fried potato) is cooked in a pan.

sentence.en: The potato is boiled in hot water.

kold.explanation: "Kold" means "cold", for weather, drinks and food, and also for people who seem unfriendly. To say you feel cold, use Jeg fryser (I am freezing), not Jeg er kold, which sounds as though you are an unfriendly person.

sentence.da: Det er en **kold** dag, og jeg fryser.
sentence.en: It is a cold day, and I am freezing.

kom nu.explanation: "Kom nu" means "come on", and literally "come now". It can encourage someone, as in Kom nu, du kan godt! (Come on, you can do it!). It can also hurry them up or show that you don't believe something.

forms.da: Kom nu, vi skal af sted.
forms.en: Come on, we have to go.

sentence.en: Come on, the bus leaves soon!

kontant.explanation: "Kontant" means "cash" or "in cash". Compare Jeg betaler kontant (I pay in cash) with Jeg betaler med kort (I pay by card). A sign saying Kun kontant means "Cash only".

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke kort og betaler **kontant**.
sentence.en: I have no card and pay in cash.

kort.explanation: "Kort" means "short", for length and for time. There is also a different word et kort, which means "a card" or "a map".

sentence.en: It is a short trip home.

kulde.explanation: "Kulde" means "cold", the low temperature itself, as in Jeg kan ikke lide kulde (I don't like the cold). Do not mix it up with kold (cold), which describes something: koldt vand (cold water).

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der sne og **kulde**.
sentence.en: In winter there is snow and cold.

kun.explanation: "Kun" means "only" or "just", and it limits the word that comes after it. Kun jeg ved det means "Only I know it", while Jeg ved kun det means "That is all I know".

sentence.en: I only have two kroner.

kvart.explanation: "Kvart" means "quarter" and is used when telling the time. Kvart over tre (a quarter past three) is 3:15, and kvart i fire (a quarter to four) is 3:45. A quarter of an hour is et kvarter (15 minutes).

sentence.en: See you at a quarter past three.

kvart i.explanation: "Kvart i" means "quarter to". Kvart i tre is 2:45, fifteen minutes before three. Do not mix it up with kvart over (quarter past): kvart over tre is 3:15.

sentence.en: The film starts at a quarter to seven.

kvart over.explanation: "Kvart over" means "quarter past". Kvart over tre is 3:15, because over means "past". Do not mix it up with kvart i (quarter to): kvart i tre is 2:45.

sentence.en: The bus comes at a quarter past eight.

kvindelig.explanation: "Kvindelig" means "female", and also "feminine", as in a feminine quality. It is built from kvinde (woman).

sentence.en: I want a female doctor.

kylling.explanation: "Kylling" means "chicken", both the bird and the meat you eat. For the meat, you say just kylling with no en in front, as in kylling med ris (chicken with rice).

sentence.en: We are eating chicken for dinner.

kærlighed.explanation: "Kærlighed" means "love", the big general word for the feeling. To say I love you, Danes use at elske (to love) instead: Jeg elsker dig (I love you).

sentence.da: Jeg elsker dig med al min **kærlighed**.
sentence.en: I love you with all my love.

kød.explanation: "Kød" means "meat", all kinds of meat as a group. To say which kind, put a word in front, as in oksekød (beef) or svinekød (pork).

sentence.en: I like eating meat and fish.

køn.explanation: "Køn" means "pretty", usually about a person, a face or a place. Do not mix it up with et køn, a different word that means "gender" (male or female).

sentence.da: Hun er en **køn** pige med langt hår.
sentence.en: She is a pretty girl with long hair.
